//: Type-checking only, the same shape orchestration/ and node-host/ use: Node 24 runs the .ts
sources by stripping types, so there is no emit step and no build artefact to keep in sync.
`erasableSyntaxOnly` refuses enums, namespaces and parameter properties — anything Node's
stripper cannot erase — so a source that type-checks is a source Node can run. This matters
here more than usual, because every L0 check drives the client through a probe that Node runs
directly from these sources.
`tools/` IS INCLUDED as well as `src/`. `tools/settled_fixture.ts` is the L1 fixture format,
recorder and player; it is NOT part of the client (it assembles a JSON-RPC envelope by hand,
which is exactly what verify_client_uses_upstream_schema forbids inside `src/`) and it is
still type-checked, because a fixture reader that has drifted from the format is the thing
the committed fixtures rest on.
`verbatimModuleSyntax` IS FALSE, AND THAT IS A DELIBERATE LOOSENING WITH A NAMED ALTERNATIVE
THAT WAS TRIED AND REJECTED. This project imports two files from `browser/` — the AVM loader
and the poseidon backend — which are dependency-free and therefore cross no npm pin. But
`browser/` has no package.json and THIS REPOSITORY HAS NO ROOT ONE, so tsc reads those files as
CommonJS and refuses their ES exports with TS1295/TS1287.
The obvious fix is a `browser/package.json` declaring `type: module`, and it WAS tried, and it
was measured safe for the sibling campaign's build. It is still rejected, because it makes
`browser/` a PACKAGE BOUNDARY for tsc, and tsc then stops applying this file's `paths` to
anything inside it — trading TS1295 for TS2307 on the poseidon backend's own imports. Turning
`verbatimModuleSyntax` off resolves both and leaves the sibling campaign's tree untouched.
WHAT IT COSTS, STATED RATHER THAN GLOSSED: tsc no longer requires `import type` for
type-only imports in this project. `erasableSyntaxOnly` — the flag that actually guarantees
Node can RUN these sources by stripping types — is untouched and still true, which is the
property `just typecheck-replay` exists to defend.
`paths` MIRRORS TWO esbuild ALIASES AND MUST STAY IN STEP WITH THEM. DD-11's poseidon
substitution redirects `@aztec/foundation/crypto/poseidon` to `browser/src/foundation_poseidon.ts`,
and that file — living in a directory with no `node_modules` — imports two `@aztec/foundation`
subpaths of its own. `build_browser_bundle.mjs` aliases exactly those two, BY SUBPATH rather
than by package (aliasing the package bypasses its `exports` map and produced 415 errors). tsc
does not read esbuild's aliases, so it needs the same two mappings or it reports TS2307 over a
file the bundler resolves perfectly well. Two spellings of one fact is a hazard; they are
adjacent and both name each other so a change to one is visible from the other. The tsc side
points at the module WITHOUT the `.js` extension so it finds `index.d.ts`; with the extension
tsc resolves the JavaScript, loses the declarations, and reports TS7016 implicit-any over a
module that is fully typed.
`skipLibCheck` is true for the same reason it is true in orchestration/: the dependencies are
@aztec/* .d.ts files whose own errors are not ours to fix, and turning it off would make this
a check about @aztec/stdlib's typings rather than about the replay client.
